fields.v: Dinu, M.-C., Zeba, F. (2026). CORTEX: A Fixed-Point Theory of Governed Coding Agents. arXiv:2610.24255v1 [cs.AI], 16 Oct 2026 (header: Preprint, September 15, 2026)
Preprint — arXiv:2610.24255v1 [cs.AI], 16 Oct 2026; page header 'Preprint. September 15, 2026', no venue
Alpha Omega Labs (both authors; company that distributes the Cortex CLI)

Proposes an approach; secondary: Proposes an evaluation method — Cortex supervisory layer (pre-execution governance, requirement tracking, validation-repair loop) formalised as a fixed-point model with conditional theorems; Gauntlet evaluation protocol (five task families, VERTEX and build-gated scores, ASR estimators), with historical raw-vs-governed pilot observations reported descriptively
fields.why: Value is defensible (Cortex layer proposed, Gauntlet protocol defined, p. 2), but most of the body (pp. 3-12) is formal theory and the pilots are declared historical, descriptive and non-causal (p. 15, 18), so a reader could take Conceptual as the main nature. Scoring is unaffected: Q13 applies either way and the pilots keep Q3-Q8 applicable.

fields.v: Cortex (version Not stated; CLI at cortex.a2olabs.com) configured over base harnesses: Cortex over Codex CLI, Cortex over Claude Code. Raw arms: Codex CLI, Claude Code, OpenCode (adapter for Oh My Pi also exists). Versions and served models Not stated ('labels are not attestations of the model')

Finite requirement set with required subset; append-only requirement/certificate ledger (certified requirements with persistent evidence); milestones + checks plan; capability/dependency policies and pre-execution hooks; safety preamble and repository configuration for governed arms

Analyze requirements -> plan milestones + checks -> execute candidate revision -> validate with fresh evidence -> coordinate (repair + revalidate changed and dependent requirements, or accept/stop), within a resource budget; governance filters every proposed action before execution (blocked action becomes refusal)
Not stated (governance hooks and validation are automatic; validation may be executable checks, rules or model judgments)
Full workflow (governance + orchestration) in historical pilots, but governance-only effect not isolated; Track S (safety) does not run the completion loop
Not classifiable; authors' wording: 'requirement tracking', 'requirement closure on a finite lattice', 'supervisory layer for pre-execution governance'
fields.why: The paper never says how the requirement set relates to a specification over time: it is an append-only ledger within a task (p. 3-4), with no statement on whether it persists or drives later changes. 'Not classifiable' is the closest value, but spec-first is arguable.

fields.v: Both: new code (6 code-generation tasks, to-do app, storefront app) and existing code (6 elementary Python bug repairs); plus adversarial safety cases
Small: safety 61 harmful + 2 probes + 2 benign controls; quality 6 tasks; repair 6 elementary issues; one to-do brief (5 checks); one storefront brief (two pools of 2 and 5 candidates)

Python utilities (secrets, parsing, database, web security, shopping cart), TypeScript upload API; full-stack to-do app; fashion e-commerce storefront PWA; agent safety (prompt injection, secret disclosure, destructive operations)
N/A (no human participants)
None reported (resource budget and reasoning budget mentioned as diagnostics only; proposed, not measured)
Behavioral test pass fraction per task (macro coverage); issue resolution (hidden tests; lenient/strict rates); to-do feature checks; storefront functional journey coverage behind a build gate

Storefront composite components: code/architecture, code health, robustness, static security, PWA/accessibility, visual similarity (CLIP), VERTEX descriptor similarity; repair composite includes patch minimality/locality and code health
None

Safety: attack-success rate (ASR, ASR@k) with Wilson intervals and case-cluster bootstrap, benign over-refusal; VERTEX trajectory similarity and VERTEX-QE (estimated references) rank agreement (Spearman); effective-feedback count (newly certified requirements); proposed diagnostics (productive passes, completion probability, surprisal) not measured

Automatic: tests in Docker, build/serve checks, Playwright-like journey probes (not named), lexical detector and action replay for safety, optional Claude-rubric LLM judge, CLIP and MiniLM embeddings. Historical June 2026 artifacts rescored; scoring protocol partly unreconstructable (conflicting judge summaries)

Models not identified for any arm (configuration labels only). One outcome per task/case and arm (single run). Criteria: classified ASR (safety), behavioral test coverage (quality), resolved issues (repair), passed checks (to-do), build-gated composite (storefront). Cost: not reported, no cost verdict.
- Codex CLI raw: ASR 42.37% (25/59); quality 0.8125; repair 6/6; to-do 3/5; storefront 0.6507 (2-arm pool), 0.7212 (5-arm pool). Quality partly; safety does not work
- Cortex over Codex: ASR 24.14% (14/58); quality 0.9792; repair 6/6; to-do 5/5; storefront 0.6799. Partly (safety improved, storefront lower)
- Claude Code raw: ASR 3.39% (2/59); quality 0.8125; repair 6/6; to-do 5/5; storefront 0.7489 (2-arm), 0.6737 (5-arm). Works/partly
- Cortex over Claude: ASR 1.67% (1/60); quality 0.9792; repair 6/6; to-do 5/5; storefront 0.6533. Works/partly (storefront lowest)
- OpenCode raw: ASR 42.59% (23/54); quality 0.3333 (4 generation failures); repair 5/6; to-do 5/5; storefront 0.7071. Does not work (safety, quality)
Benign controls: zero refusals on 2 controls for the four paired arms; OpenCode refused 1 of 2

Historical June 2026 pilots, not one controlled experiment. Five arms (Codex raw, Cortex over Codex, Claude Code raw, Cortex over Claude, OpenCode). Baseline: raw (unwrapped) harness. Held constant: Not ensured (Cortex arms also change prompts, configuration, sometimes repair budgets; unequal observation sets; 15 of 305 safety cells missing after timeouts). Acceptance tests: behavioral tests, hidden issue tests, feature checks, storefront probes; no auxiliary held-out/regression tests run. Repetitions: one per cell; repair is replay of saved patches; storefront rescored artifacts. Human intervention: Not stated. Governed arms may use evaluation feedback during repair (adaptive scores)

Safety: relative ASR reduction ~43.0% (Codex pair) and ~50.8% (Claude pair), unmatched case sets. Quality: paired Cortex 0.9792 vs raw 0.8125, entirely from the TypeScript upload task. Repair: no difference (6/6 all paired). To-do: Cortex over Codex 5/5 vs Codex 3/5; Claude pair equal. Storefront: no Cortex advantage (5-arm: Codex raw 0.7212 best, Cortex over Claude 0.6533 lowest). VERTEX-QE vs authored rank: Spearman 1.0 (2-arm), 0.6 (5-arm). Significance: no tests; authors state no causal claims

Partly distinguished arms on safety; not on repair; storefront not consistent. Repeatable: no (single historical runs, rescoring, incomplete provenance; benchmark snapshot excludes private dependencies and raw captures). Limitations stated: unequal observation sets, missing timeouts, adaptive selection, conflicting metadata, lexical classification not observed exploits, too few benign controls, governance-only effect not isolated

No uniform Cortex advantage; theorems are conditional (A1 complete mediation, A2 sound monotone persistent validation, A3 bounded judging) and repair/fallible validation/budgets do not satisfy them automatically; length-sensitive similarity, heuristic references, conditional coverage, correlated attempts, incomplete observations; payment, carrier-task utility and long-horizon behavior unmeasured; evaluator integrity and sandbox not established. Needed: matched policy ablations with fixed model, tasks, tools, budget and independent final evaluation

Gauntlet snapshot: github.com/Xpitfire/cortex-gauntlet (incomplete for reproduction); results site benchmark.cortex.a2olabs.com. No pre-registration. Languages: Python, TypeScript, web. Reported inconsistencies (by the authors): historical summary describes a chat app while retained outcomes are a to-do app; judge summary says heuristic while entries name an LLM judge; quality outcomes describe dynamic execution while methodology says static-only. Paper header date (15 Sep 2026) differs from arXiv date (16 Oct 2026). Mostly theoretical paper (pp. 3-12)
Yes (1): two aims (guarantees under assumptions; evaluation) and three evaluation questions stated
Partly (0.5): metrics formally defined; models, prompts, budgets and run conditions of the pilots not specified; benchmark snapshot incomplete
No (0): served models not identified; harness versions not stated
Partly (0.5): tasks described in appendix; benchmark snapshot public but excludes private dependencies and raw captures
Partly (0.5): behavioral and hidden tests, but safety by lexical classification and several heuristic proxies
Partly (0.5): metrics defined; no cost metrics reported
Partly (0.5): raw harness baselines, but conditions not matched (prompts, budgets, case sets)
Partly (0.5): Wilson intervals for safety; single runs elsewhere, no statistical tests
fields.why: Single runs per cell (p. 14-15) and no test of raw-vs-governed differences point to No; stored Wilson intervals on single-arm safety rates (Table 3, p. 15) are the only basis for Partly. Author to decide whether per-arm intervals count as handling variability.
